name: Familial Lipoprotein Lipase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Lipoprotein Lipase Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of severe hyperchylomicronemia with fasting triglycerides >2000 mg/dL
Demonstrated deficiency or absence of lipoprotein lipase enzyme activity in plasma or post-heparin plasma
Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomas, and lipemia retinalis
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the LPL gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe hyperchylomicronemia with fasting triglycerides >2000 mg/dL plus either deficient lipoprotein lipase activity or characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Markedly elevated triglycerides due to chylomicron accumulation
searchTerms: extremely high blood fat after fasting

pathognomonic.notes: Yellowish papules typically on extensor surfaces
Milky appearance of retinal blood vessels

common.symptomName: Recurrent abdominal pain due to pancreatitis
common.notes: Episodes often triggered by high-fat meals
searchTerms: episodic abdominal pain due to pancreas inflammation

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to lipid accumulation
Poor weight gain and growth delay
searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby
neurological issues secondary to pancreas inflammation

occasional.notes: Sensory deficits possibly related to recurrent pancreatitis
Milky or turbid plasma after fasting
Secondary diabetes due to pancreatic damage

rare.notes: Accumulation of chylous fluid in the peritoneal cavity
Rare ischemic events possibly related to hyperviscosity
searchTerms: central nervous system problems including stroke

laboratory: Low or absent post-heparin lipoprotein lipase activity
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing pancreatitis or pancreatic pseudocysts
other: Milky appearance of serum after fasting

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of apolipoprotein C-II instead of lipoprotein lipase
Similar biochemical profile but different genetic cause
Later onset and less severe pancreatitis risk

redFlags: Severe hypertriglyceridemia (>2000 mg/dL) in infancy or childhood
Presence of eruptive xanthomas and lipemia retinalis
references: Goldberg IJ. Familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency: clinical and biochemical features. J Lipid Res. 2017.
Orphanet: Familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency. ORPHA:309015.
Hegele RA. Genetic lipoprotein lipase deficiency. GeneReviews. 2020.
